title: Evaluation of WAEVE® Pre-Measurement Feature for Detection of Implanted Coronary Stents in Patients Undergoing Elective PCI
official: Evaluation of WAEVE® Pre-Measurement Feature for Detection of Implanted Coronary Stents in Patients Undergoing Elective PCI: NIMBLE-II Study
summary:
Coronary stent implantation is a common treatment for coronary artery disease. However, current methods used to evaluate implanted stents and detect complications such as in-stent restenosis are generally invasive and may require ionizing radiation.

The WAEVE® device is an investigational, non-invasive, non-ionizing medical device that uses microwave interferometry to assess implanted coronary stents. The NIMBLE-II study is designed to evaluate the performance of a new pre-measurement feature incorporated into WAEVE® that detects heartbeat-synchronous microwave reflections and helps distinguish true stent-related signals from non-cardiac or artifactual signals. By confirming the cardiac origin of the detected reflection, this feature is intended to improve the robustness and reliability of WAEVE® measurements and reduce the risk of false detections arising from non-cardiac or artifactual reflections.

This prospective, multicenter, single-arm clinical investigation will enroll adults undergoing elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Participants will undergo WAEVE® measurements before PCI and, when a single coronary stent is implanted, after PCI. The study aims to generate technical and clinical evidence supporting the reliability and robustness of the WAEVE® pre-measurement feature under real clinical conditions.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults ≥18 years of age.
* scheduled for a PCI procedure with potential stent implantation and without any previously implanted coronary stent.
* Clinically stable condition allowing completion of pre-PCI WAEVE® measurements.
* Ability to understand the study procedures and provide written informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Hemodynamic instability, cardiogenic shock, or severe arrhythmias.
* Active implantable electronic devices or metallic implants on the chest that may interfere with measurements (e.g., pacemakers, defibrillators, CRT devices, sternal wires, rib plates, metallic clips).
* Presence of skin conditions, wounds, or lesions in the areas designated for transducer placement (including extensive thoracic skin lesions).
* Inability to remain supine or still during WAEVE® measurements.
* Pregnancy or absence of a negative pregnancy test in women of childbearing potential.
